sources.title: Split Ducted Units - Airflow Application Guidelines, Doc 0520-026 Ver.1
sources.basis: Manufacturer design guideline for VAF (Advance) split ducted, EVV/EFV140-240S
sources.notes: Ideal duct static 125 Pa for VAF vs 150-250 Pa for standard systems. Final duct max 3 m/s, return duct max 4 m/s, main 6-7 m/s, branch 4-6 m/s. Per-model nominal and minimum supply L/s. Balance at branch take-offs, not at outlets.

sources.title: Installation Best Practice Guidelines - Ducted Type Systems (DB0817 Builders booklet v1.7)
sources.notes: Flex duct table: maximum recommended L/s by flex diameter 100-550 mm. Total external static 125 Pa recommended for VFT; commissioning check that it does not exceed 250 Pa. The last zone left on must suit the unit's minimum airflow. Flex hung at most every 1500 mm with at most 40 mm sag (cites AS 4254).

sources.title: AirTouch 4 Installer Manual (s5.6-5.7 Minimum ventilation; Spill or Bypass)
sources.notes: Spill groups stay open whenever the AC runs. Spill dampers modulate so total opening is 100% (1 spill group) or 200% (2 groups). Max spill groups = half the groups; avoid bedrooms; at least one spill group unless there is a permanently open zone. Bypass port is fully open or fully closed only.

sources.title: AirTouch 5 Installer Manual (s5.5 Spill/Bypass)
sources.notes: Same rule as AT4: the chosen spill zones stay fully open while the AC runs (2 spill zones = at least 2 zones fully open); max spill zones = half the zones; one bypass damper per AC.

sources.title: AirTouch / Zonemaster Zone Control System Installation Manual
sources.notes: Spill/bypass set-point is a % of open zones against total zones. Factory default 30%, adjustable 0-50% in 10% steps (e.g. 8 zones x 30% = 2.4, so 3 zones). Low-numbered zones near the return grille open first. Do not use 0% without a permanently open zone. Balancing range 10-100%.

sources.title: Polyaire Diffusion Fitting (PDF) product page
sources.notes: Inlet 350 or 400 mm. Splits into 2, 3 or 4 outlets of 250-300 mm. Outlets take manual or Zonemaster dampers. No L/s or pressure data.

sources.title: Zone Controller PAC-ZC40/80L/H-E Installation Manual (BH79D480H01)
sources.notes: A common (always open) zone is recommended. Without one, spill zones must be set and open automatically when all zones close. The installer enters the outlet count per zone (and common zone) for the auto fan. All outlets should have equal static pressure. No % figures.

sources.title: Zone Station II (I-ZSII) installation instructions
sources.notes: Can be set to 0, 1 or 2 programmed constant zones. The system keeps at least 1 (zone 1) or at least 2 (zones 1+2) zones open. Up to 6 zones.

sources.title: MyAir5 User Guide (Constant Zones)
sources.notes: The installer may enable 1, 2 or 3 constant zones depending on system size and home design. They open to relieve excess pressure when too few zones are open. MyZone becomes the first constant. Damper 5% steps.

sources.title: Ducted quote: Zone 10 / MyAir 4 + General Information, Terms and Conditions
sources.basis: Installer practice (dealer quote T&Cs, reproduces Advantage Air marketing)
sources.notes: Up to 14 kW: keep at least 2-3 outlets open on low fan to limit noise. 14-25 kW: at least 3-4 outlets. A single outlet is not recommended. Advantage Air marketing says a legacy dump zone can be up to 25% of the home.

sources.title: StarPro SP4/SP5/SP6 & BX5 Ducted Gas Heater Installer's Manual
sources.basis: Manufacturer installation manual (gas ducted heating, add-on cooling)
sources.notes: Minimum fully open outlets (150 mm ceiling diffusers): 5-7 without adaptive zoning, 1.5-3 with Networker adaptive zoning (the fan slows). Max ceiling outlets 10-17. Airflow rated at 125 Pa for 30/35 models and 50 Pa for others. Basebox spigots 300-450 mm. Zoning cooling minimum fan 1000 RPM. Temperature rise limit 45 K.

sources.title: Myzone Multipoint 56 Wall Switch installation manual
sources.notes: Spill zones keep enough airflow across the indoor coil. The number of spill zones sets the minimum zones that must be on; the control forces them on. No %.

sources.title: Ducted Air Conditioner Operation Manual FDYQN
sources.notes: Owner and installer must confirm the minimum number or combination of zones that must be on before starting. No number given.

sources.title: Guide Sheet: Flexible Ducting Installation for Small Ducted Units (Pamphlet 2203)
sources.basis: Manufacturer lab tests, 250 mm flex at 4.5 m/s
sources.notes: Never use duct smaller than the unit spigot. Step up a size for runs over 3 m. Do not blank an outlet at the spigot plate. Outlet area must be at least the original area. Avoid short plenums with side outlets near draw-through units; long plenums are better (diagram labels about 4 duct diameters). Bend radius at least 1.5D. Measured losses at 4.5 m/s: 90 deg bend 10 Pa (1.5R) or 18 Pa (0.5R); 180 deg 12/28 Pa; S-bend 30/65 Pa; diffuser entry 16 Pa (side) / 21 Pa (top, supported) / 53 Pa (top, kinked); 3 m of 250 mm = 9 Pa; 6 m of 300 mm = 8 Pa.

sources.title: NCC 2022 Volume One, Part J6, clause J6D5 Fan and duct systems
sources.basis: National code, deemed-to-satisfy (Class 2-9 buildings; not Class 1 houses)
sources.notes: Index run average at most 1 Pa/m (flex calculated as laid straight). Flex at most 6 m in any run. Index-run component maxima: balancing/control damper fully open 25 Pa, fire damper 15 Pa, VAV box 25 Pa, supply diffuser/grille 40 Pa, exhaust grille 30 Pa, transfer duct 12 Pa, door grille 12 Pa, attenuator 40 Pa. Filters clean: MERV9 55, MERV11 65, MERV13 95, MERV14 110 Pa. Coils: 1-row 30 up to 10-row 220 Pa. Exempt: unducted systems under 1000 L/s.

sources.title: NCC 2025 Fan and duct system - worked example / guidance
sources.notes: NCC 2025 moves the flex length limit to J6D5(8) and extends the fitting-size rule to all fittings. Adds max drops for relief/exhaust louvres and door undercuts. Index-run fan pressure must assume dirty filters. Example FCU duty points 230-255 Pa.

sources.title: Worksection 0741p Ductwork (ALP International branded) - Ductwork selection guidance
sources.page: Selection / Design guidance; Flexible duct commentary
sources.notes: Suggested rigid ductwork: velocity at most 6 m/s and loss at most 1 Pa/m. Flexible duct: velocity at most 4 m/s; at most 6 m between fan and furthest outlet. A flex at 70% extension has about 10x the loss, at 90% about 3x. Splitter dampers only on branches up to 300 mm with main velocity under 10 m/s.

sources.title: Skills Workshop Module 22 - Basics of Duct Design (Siganto & Mason; Ahern rules)
sources.basis: Industry body training article (Ahern 1977 rules; DA3)
sources.notes: Low-pressure sizing: under 180 L/s use 4.5 m/s; 180-4500 L/s use 1.2 Pa/m; over 4500 L/s use 10 m/s. Flex runouts limited to 3.5 m/s, with friction taken at twice the measured length. A cushion-head box costs at least 1.5 velocity heads (Pv = 0.6 v^2).

sources.title: Skills Workshop Module 23 - Flexible ductwork installation
sources.notes: Bend centreline radius at least 1 duct diameter. Excess length under 5%. Run straight at least 300 mm out of plenums, junctions and boots before bending. Support at most every 1.5 m horizontally; sag at most 25 mm per 300 mm.

sources.title: AIRAH response to NCC 2025 Public Comment Draft (J6)
sources.notes: AIRAH calls 1 Pa/m very high. Designers were taught at most 0.8 Pa/m, preferably lower. 1 Pa/m was meant as a minimum standard.

sources.title: Section J Case Study series: Ductwork (peer-reviewed technical paper)
sources.notes: Meeting the NCC 1 Pa/m straight-duct DtS gives about 5 m/s (4.4-5.4 m/s in the examples). Aspect ratio 4:1 recommended max (DA03 allows 8:1).

sources.title: AS 4254 Ductwork Construction Guide (design memo)
sources.notes: AS 4254.1 flex: design pressure 1000 Pa positive / 200 Pa negative; single run at most 6 m, fully extended, no intermediate joints. AS 4254.2 leakage at most 5% at 1.25x pressure for systems of 3000 L/s or more.

sources.title: ACCA's Manual D Residential Duct Design Checklist / 'Verifying ACCA Manual D Procedures' (incl. Manual D Table 3-1)
sources.page: p.2 (Friction Rate Worksheet; Recommended Velocity table)
sources.notes: Supply trunk: rigid 700 fpm recommended / 900 max; flex 600 / 700. Supply branch: rigid 600 / 900; flex 600 / 700. Return trunk 600 / 700; return branch 400 / 700. Standard device losses 0.03 IWC for supply outlet, return grille and balancing damper. Worked example: filter 0.18, DX coil 0.23, ESP 0.70, ASP 0.20 IWC. Friction 0.10 IWC/100 ft, acceptable chart range 0.06-0.18.

sources.title: ASHRAE Handbook 1972 Table 6 'Recommended and maximum duct velocities for low velocity systems' in 'Green HVAC Ductwork Done Right' (Smithart & Reints)
sources.notes: Residences: main ducts 700-900 fpm, branch ducts 600 fpm, branch risers 500 fpm.

sources.title: ASHRAE Handbook Fundamentals Ch.21 Duct Design: friction-rate range and Table 12 acoustic velocity limits, in AMCA 'VAV Systems Part 2: VAV System Duct Design'
sources.notes: Low-pressure friction typically 0.05-0.20 IWC/100 ft. Max velocity above a solid drywall ceiling: RC25 or less, 1500 fpm rectangular / 2500 round; RC35, 2500/3500. Above a suspended ceiling, RC25: 1000/2000. Duct in occupied space, RC25: 950/1700. Handbook notes: branches about 80% of these, final runouts about 50%.

sources.title: HVAC Systems Duct Design, 4th Edition
sources.page: s5.9 (Ex 5-11 SI), s5.10.4, s7.3.2, Table A-1, NC/RC table
sources.notes: Common low-pressure friction 0.1 IWC/100 ft = 0.8-1.0 Pa/m (modified equal friction). SI example: 200 L/s at 0.9 Pa/m gives 250 mm at 4.2 m/s; later run 250 L/s gives 270 mm at 4.6 m/s. All flexible duct is in the 'rough' category when fully extended, with extra correction for compression. Example 10 in. diffuser at 440 cfm = 0.12 IWC. Residences NC/RC 20-35.

sources.title: Comfort Zone II Zoning System Design Guide (Form ZONEKIT-2XA, Cat. 809-522)
sources.notes: Zone duct areas give about 0.1 IWC/100 ft with sheet metal at most 900 fpm (mains) and 700 fpm (branches). Duct board areas x1.1, flex x1.25. Supply traditionally 0.1, return 0.08 IWC/100 ft. Zoned ducts oversized 25-30%. Bypass needed if the smallest zone plus controlled leakage cannot take 60% of nominal CFM. Zones under 20% of total CFM get about 10% more area. 6 in. pipe carries 100 CFM and 8 in. 240 CFM at 0.1 IWC.

sources.title: Zoning System Design Manual 70-2321-03
sources.notes: No zone smaller than about 25% of system CFM. Ducts designed normally at 0.10 or 0.08 IWC/100 ft. Zone damper at least 6 ft from a diffuser and 3 ft from the plenum. Bypass CFM = total CFM - smallest zone CFM. Variable-speed fan: DS terminal drops blower speed when 1 zone calls (or under 25% of capacity on systems with more than 4 zones).

sources.title: Zoning Design and Application Guide - HVAC Zoning Systems
sources.notes: Size each zone duct for about 2/3 of system CFM so it can take the unit's CFM alone. At least five 6 in. take-offs per zone or equivalent. Zone duct vs system CFM: 800 and 1000 cfm 12 in., 1200 and 1400 cfm 14 in., 1600 cfm 16 in., 2000 cfm 18 in. Blower rating usually 0.5 IWC. Two-zone commercial can skip bypass if each zone duct handles 60-70% of total. Barometric bypass up to 3000 CFM; motorised + SP control above 4000 CFM.

sources.title: Zoning Duct Design Guide for Mechanical System Designers v1.0 (M154-116/2017E)
sources.notes: Low velocity: TESP at most 0.5 in (125 Pa). Supply trunk at most 900 fpm (4.57 m/s) at design. Zone trunks carrying under 50% of system airflow are noise-tested as if carrying 50%. Return trunk 700 fpm, return branch 650 fpm. Zone load bands: 2 zones 40-60%, 3 zones 23-43%, 4 zones 15-35% of total. Prefer modulating equipment; avoid bypass (option C).

sources.title: Manual Zr Residential Zoning, 1st Ed. Version 1.10 (public review draft)
sources.page: s6-8 Zone dampers, s7/8 bypass airway
sources.basis: Industry standard (review draft, not final text)
sources.notes: Bypass airway sized at 900 fpm (Manual Zr default). An open zone damper may run 800-1000 fpm. A linear modulating damper needs about 20% of the circulation-path pressure drop when open (so over 900 fpm). Vendor bypass rules up to 1400 fpm. Default low-limit discharge temperature 45 F. The critical zone is the smallest-CFM zone. Bypass factor = bypass CFM / blower CFM, capped by the safe limit or the AHJ limit, whichever is lower.

sources.title: Managing Airflow in Zoned Applications
sources.basis: Manufacturer technical article (ACCA Manual Zr method)
sources.notes: Typical catalogue bypass: 12 in. round for 1000 CFM (1300 fpm). A short bypass short-circuits, so balance it with a hand damper to the same pressure drop as the longest zone run. Bypass factor example 50%.

sources.publisher: Proctor Engineering Group (for CA IOU Codes & Standards)
sources.title: Zoning Ducted Air Conditioners, Heat Pumps, and Furnaces: Summary of a Case Study (H114)
sources.notes: Carrier lab: 50% bypass cuts efficiency to 77%. ACCA Manual Zr equation: about 31% lower sensible capacity at 50% bypass. Field: 31% bypass gave 25% capacity loss. Zoned systems averaged 292 CFM/ton. Supports the CA rule of at least 350 CFM/ton and at most 0.58 W/CFM in every zonal mode.

sources.publisher: California Energy Commission (via Energy Code Ace / ACHR News)
sources.title: 2022 Building Energy Efficiency Standards s150.0(m)13 & s150.1(c)13 - zonally controlled systems
sources.notes: Zonally controlled central forced-air cooling must deliver more than 350 CFM/ton in every zonal control mode (fan efficacy at most 0.45 W/cfm gas furnace or 0.58 other). Bypass ducts into the return are not allowed unless the compliance certificate says otherwise. Variable-speed systems may show compliance at max speed with all zones calling.

sources.title: Harmony III Zoning System Installation Instructions
sources.notes: Keep zone CFM within 25% of the average (within 10% for 'equal' zones). Variable-speed blower minimum CFM for zoning: about 250 for 2-3 ton, 380 for 4 ton, 450 for 5 ton air handlers; 426-523 for some 3-ton furnaces.

sources.title: SmartZone Damper Guide / What size dampers do I need?
sources.notes: Keep damper air velocity about 600-700 fpm, never above 900 fpm. Upsize the duct and damper one size for each zone under 25% of system airflow. With single-speed equipment, at most 3 zones and none under 20% of equipment CFM.

sources.title: Duct School Reference Guide (supply/return size-capacity; fitting equivalent lengths)
sources.notes: Size table stated at 0.09-0.10 IWC per 100 ft EL. Plenum take-off equivalent lengths: offset starting collar 10 ft, straight starting collar 35 ft, round starting collar 35 ft; 90 deg round elbow 30 ft. Capacities check about 15-25% above a 0.1 IWC/100 ft friction chart.

sources.title: Air Velocity Quick Tips
sources.notes: Residential main ducts 700-900 fpm, branch ducts 500-700 fpm. Return grille face 500 fpm or less.

sources.title: Sizing Ducts - recommended velocities
sources.notes: Comfort systems: main 4-7 m/s, main branch 3-5 m/s, branch 1-3 m/s.

sources.title: Ducted Range brochure
sources.notes: Rated external static ranges: slim 0-90 Pa; mid static 30-150 or 50-150 Pa; high static 30-200, 60-210, 60-260 Pa. VAV zone damper 0-100% in 5% steps. No minimum airflow or spill figures.

Each zone trunk must carry 50% of system airflow at <=4.57 m/s ('noise test').

Systems >13 kW: 2 or more outlets in the minimum zone. Consider two outlets on any minimum-zone selection.

1 spill group: spill dampers keep the sum of open damper % at 100% or more (one full zone equivalent); 2 groups = 200%. Max spill groups = half of groups.

Installer confirms the minimum zone count/combination before start-up.
The last zone on (smallest zone) must pass the unit's minimum supply airflow through correctly sized outlets.
Bypass CFM = total CFM - smallest-zone CFM. Static-pressure-regulated bypass. With VS fans, use bypass with SP control.
Bypass/dump if the smallest zone plus leakage takes under 60% of nominal CFM.
Prefer equipment that modulates airflow/capacity (A), then leakage to non-calling zones (B); avoid bypass (C).
Critical zone = smallest-CFM zone; bypass factor capped by safe and AHJ limits; low-limit 45 F discharge.
Balance the bypass to the same pressure drop as the longest zone run (hand damper), or it short-circuits.
50% bypass costs about 23% efficiency (Carrier lab) or about 31% sensible capacity (ACCA eqn); 31% bypass cost 25% capacity in the field.
No bypass ducts (prescriptive). More than 350 CFM/ton in every zonal mode; fan at most 0.58 W/cfm (0.45 gas furnace).
Marketing claim: a legacy permanently-open dump zone can be up to 25% of the home. Low confidence.
